newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALPINE SKIING-GERG ACHIEVES GOAL IN EUROPEAN OPENER.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-GERG ACHIEVES GOAL IN EUROPEAN OPENER.

text.p: Hilde Gerg achieved her season's goal in the very first World Cup ski race of the 1996-97 European circuit with an impressive super-G victory over fellow German Katja Seizinger on Thursday.

"It was my main objective this season to win a second World Cup victory at last. I had been waiting for that moment for nearly two years," she said after beating her prestigious compatriot by 0.39 of a second.

"I had posted a number of podium places this season and I'm relieved it's here at last. I think my improvement in downhills helped a lot," added the skier from Lenggries dubbed "Wilde Hilde" by her team mates.
"She deserved the nickname today," said Seizinger, winner of the three races held in the French resort last year.
"To win by such a margin is really impressive. As for me, I haven't been at my best in super-G's yet so a second place is a morale-booster."
Second place helped the overall World Cup holder and leader retain her lead over Pernilla Wiberg by 494 points to 382. Gerg, third, has 376.
Isolde Kostner of Italy, third in the race and fourth overall, warned she may be a much tougher challenger in the weeks to come.
"I'm not at my best yet and I don't expect to reach my best before January. To finish third in these conditions is brilliant," she said.

Sweden's Wiberg, only ninth, appeared to be in the best form of her life in the races held in the U.S. in recent weeks -- she had won the season's opening super-G and taken second place in the second.
"I just made too many mistakes. That's all," she said.
Gerg, who scored her first World Cup victory in a super-G in Sierra Nevada in 1994, was the only starter to finish under the 1:08 barrier on the OK piste.
She clocked 1:07.81, with Seizinger second on 1:08.20 and Kostner 0.18 further behind.
The outcome was hardly a surprise as Gerg had already taken third place in one of two super-G's won by Seizinger here last year. Kostner had also taken second place in one of them.
If the podium looked familiar, the weather was unusually sunny for a mid-December in Savoy, making the course faster and favouring specialists.
The race was marred by an accident in which French front runner Jenny Vallier lost balance on a bump just before the finish and crashed into three photographers.
She was taken to hospital with a lung injury but it was not immediatly clear how serious it was, according to medical sources.
One of the photographers broke a leg in the accident which delayed the start of the race for half an hour.
It was the fifth consecutive victory by a German in the French resort. Martina Ertl won a giant slalom two years ago.

The Germans will again be among the favourites in Friday's giant slalom. Italian Sabina Panzanini won the inaugural giant slalom of the season in Park City, Utah, last month ahead of Austria's Anita Wachter and Seizinger.
